subject: SIG question — privileged access & backup encryption (interpretation requested)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@velocitech.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG question — privileged access & backup encryption (interpretation requested)

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for sending over VelociTech's SIG. We started working through the questionnaire and bumped into two items that feel ambiguous from our side; rather than guess, I wanted to confirm your intent so our answers match your review expectations.

The two questions:
1)  A Privileged Accounts/control question (SIG section ~5.x): wording asks to "describe controls restricting and monitoring privileged accounts." It's not explicit whether this is intended to include vendor/third-party platform operator access (i.e., Redwood engineers/infra team access to the customers' tenant/VMs) or only customer-owned IAM (end-user/admin accounts). For our answer we can either:
   - include both (describe Redwood operator access controls + how customers control their own admins), or
   - limit the scope to customer-owned accounts only.

2)  Backup encryption (SIG section ~12.x): the question asks whether backups are encrypted and references "customer-managed keys (CMKs)". That could be read two ways:
   - Are you able to support CMKs (i.e., customers can provide keys and we will use them), or
   - Are backups encrypted with any managed keys and we should indicate whether they are Redwood-managed KMS keys?

We've attached a draft mapping (20260220_SIG_mapping_draft.xlsx) showing our proposed short answers and suggested evidence to attach. Also included is a small diagram of our privileged access model (architecture-privileged-access.png).

Could you let us know which interpretation you prefer for each item? If it's easier, we can jump on a short call — I'm available Mon/Tue next week afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
From: Olivia Park <olivia@velocitech.com>

Subject: Re: SIG question — privileged access & backup encryption (interpretation requested)

Hi Soojin,

Appreciate the précis and the attachments — that helps. Quick answers:
- For the privileged accounts item, VelociTech expects the vendor to document the controls we can reasonably review during security assessment (so include Redwood operator access controls, but please label which controls apply to Redwood staff vs customer-admin functions). We need enough detail to confirm least-privilege, MFA, and monitoring/alerting for vendor accounts.
- For backups, we want to know both: whether backups are encrypted at rest (and in transit) and whether you support CMKs as an option. If CMKs are only supported in certain deployment modes, please call that out explicitly.

Would it be possible to get a short written update today/tomorrow reflecting that framing? We can then decide whether a call is needed. If we still have follow-ups, I'll schedule a 30-min sync.

Thanks —
Olivia
Senior Information Security Manager\VelociTech
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 13:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG question — privileged access & backup encryption (interpretation requested)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the quick direction. Below is a concise written interpretation we can include in the SIG answers (we'll also update the attached spreadsheet):

1) Privileged accounts (vendor vs customer scope) — interpretation for VelociTech:
   - Include vendor/operator accounts in the response. Label clearly which controls are Redwood-operated (e.g., operator jump-host access, privileged role separation) and which are customer-managed.
   - For vendor/operator controls, we'll provide:
     * Authentication & MFA requirements for operator accounts (okta + hardware 2FA),
     * Just-in-time (JIT) elevation and time-limited access for sensitive systems,
     * Session recording and audit log retention policy (90 days),
     * Quarterly access reviews with customer-designated approvers.

2) Backups & CMKs — interpretation for VelociTech:
   - State that backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
   - Indicate that Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and via cloud KMS integrations for Dedicated contracts; hosted API (default) uses Redwood-managed keys unless a dedicated/enterprise arrangement is in place.
   - We'll point to evidence: our encryption whitepaper section, KMS integration docs, and a sample key usage log (redacted).

We'll add short evidence pointers in the spreadsheet and include the architecture diagram. If that matches your expectations, we'll mark these as our official SIG answers and attach the evidence links.

Flagging to Michael and Evelyn in case you want to add any SOC2 control IDs or alternate wording.

Best,
Soojin

--

Thanks — this is helpful. I reviewed the proposed wording and it aligns with VelociTech's expectations. A couple small follow-ups:

- Please make the CMK sentence explicit that CMK functionality is not available on Redwood's hosted public API tier; it is available for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) customers.
- For the vendor/operator controls, can you provide one example evidence artifact for session recording (e.g., sample audit log with timestamps redacted)? If you can drop that into the Drive folder today, procurement can accept the answer and move to the next review step.

I've attached an updated SIG spreadsheet (sig_answer_v1.xlsx) where I noted a few editorial tweaks (two-line comments). If you could incorporate those and confirm the updated files are in the Drive link you provided, we'll mark this item as satisfied.

If anything is tricky, we can do a 20-min call — but I think a written update will be fine.

Regards,
Olivia
